title: Why Ford Could Be Sued Where the Crash Happened
content:
A Ford Explorer first sold in Washington ended up in Montana. A Ford Crown Victoria first sold in North Dakota ended up in Minnesota. Both vehicles were involved in serious crashes, and both lawsuits raised a question about their history. Could the courts in the states where the crashes happened hear claims against Ford when Ford had first sold those particular cars elsewhere? [U.S. Supreme Court opinion in Ford](https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/20pdf/19-368_febh.pdf)

The U.S. Supreme Court said yes on the facts of these two cases. In its March 25, 2021 decision in *Ford Motor Co. v. Montana Eighth Judicial District Court*, it considered Ford's business in each state and how that business related to the claims. The first-sale receipt mattered to Ford's argument. The rest of the record explained why that receipt did not settle the jurisdiction question. [Supreme Court opinion, 592 U.S. 351, slip opinion pp. 1–4, 8–14](https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/20pdf/19-368_febh.pdf)

## Two vehicles and two routes into court

The Montana case involved a 1996 Explorer. A rear tire's tread separated, the vehicle rolled, and the driver died. Her estate sued in Montana, alleging a design defect, a failure to warn, and negligence. In Minnesota, a 1994 Crown Victoria hit a snowplow. A passenger was seriously injured when the airbag did not deploy. He brought claims in Minnesota over the vehicle and the collision. [U.S. Supreme Court opinion in Ford](https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/20pdf/19-368_febh.pdf)

Ford had designed and manufactured both vehicles outside the two states where the lawsuits were filed. It argued that its contacts with each state did not cause the injury because the particular vehicles had arrived there through resale and relocation. The plaintiffs also had evidence about Ford's ongoing efforts to sell, advertise, and service the same models in the states where the respective crashes occurred. [*Ford*, slip opinion pp. 2–5](https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/20pdf/19-368_febh.pdf)

## Why the market for the model mattered

Personal jurisdiction is a court's authority over a defendant. The question here was **specific jurisdiction**, which links that authority to the claims in the particular lawsuit. The Court looked for a relationship between Ford's activities in each state and the dispute there. Ford served the in-state market for the models, the victims were residents, and the crashes and injuries occurred in those states. [U.S. Supreme Court opinion in Ford](https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/20pdf/19-368_febh.pdf)

The Court rejected the need for a strict causal chain from Ford's in-state business to the initial sale of the particular vehicle in these circumstances. The majority emphasized that the relationship still has limits. The case supports looking beyond a vehicle's first sale when there is a meaningful connection between the defendant's forum activities and the dispute. [*Ford*, slip opinion pp. 6–15](https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/20pdf/19-368_febh.pdf)

Jurisdiction clears a threshold to litigating the claims. The proof of a defect, the connection between the alleged defect and the injury, and the amount of any damages are questions for the merits. Keep evidence for those questions in a separate part of the file.

## Organize the evidence around three different questions

**Where can the dispute be heard?** Preserve documents showing where the accident happened and where the vehicle was sold, resold, registered, and serviced. Record what is known about the manufacturer's business involving that model in the relevant state. Each defendant's contacts and role may require separate analysis.

**What happened to this vehicle?** Record the VIN, model, build date if available, component identifiers, repair history, and condition before and after the crash. Photos and inspection records can help track which tire, restraint, sensor, or other component was present at the time. Get guidance on preserving the vehicle and components before repair, dismantling, or disposal when a defect is at issue.

**What supports the proposed defect explanation?** A recall lookup is a starting point for identifying campaigns. NHTSA describes what its VIN search displays and what it can omit, including previously completed recalls. A campaign affecting a model may call for checking the precise VIN and component, repair history, and whether the concern matches the failure being investigated. [NHTSA recall search and its coverage notes](https://www.nhtsa.gov/recalls)

## A used-car receipt is part of the record

Imagine a driver buys a used car in State A and later moves to State B, where the manufacturer sells and services that model. If a crash happens in State B, a receipt from State A documents how the particular car got to the driver. Separate evidence about State B may show the connection between that market, the model, and the claimed injury. The analysis changes if the manufacturer had little relevant connection to the state or the underlying accident occurred elsewhere.

The value of the two Ford cases is the separation of these records. Where this car traveled, what the manufacturer did in the state, and what happened to this component are each factual questions. A single report is rarely the best source for all three.

Use the [Evidence-to-Fact Map](/tools/evidence-to-fact-map) to attach one source to each entry in a vehicle history. Keep a distinct row for the alleged failure and for the evidence connecting it to the injury.

## Keep the vehicle history beside the alleged component failure

Create one file for the chain of sale, registration, and service and another for evidence about the particular part. A service invoice can show where and when maintenance took place. A VIN lookup can identify some unrepaired recalls. Neither record alone identifies what caused a component to fail. The Supreme Court's jurisdiction ruling and NHTSA's recall search describe different questions. [U.S. Supreme Court opinion in Ford](https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/20pdf/19-368_febh.pdf) · [NHTSA recall lookup](https://www.nhtsa.gov/recalls)

The [Accident Photo Checklist](/tools/photo-documentation-planner) can help organize photographs of the vehicle and relevant components. If the evidence includes recorded vehicle data, see [how to keep event clocks separate](/articles/why-time-zero-matters-in-a-truck-crash-black-box-report). The [car crash checklist](/articles/what-to-do-after-a-car-accident-a-complete-step-by-step-guide) explains how to preserve original photos, reports, and witness records alongside the vehicle's history.

## Read the record

- [U.S. Supreme Court, *Ford Motor Co. v. Montana Eighth Judicial District Court*, Nos. 19-368 and 19-369, March 25, 2021](https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/20pdf/19-368_febh.pdf)
- [NHTSA, recall lookup and information about results](https://www.nhtsa.gov/recalls)

title: DUI Accident Claims: Evidence, Damages, and Insurance
content:
A DUI arrest can give an insurance claim a clear investigative starting point. The police may have observations, test results, and witness accounts that are unavailable after many other crashes. You still need a separate record of how the crash happened, what it cost, and which policy applies. A criminal fine goes through the criminal process. A civil claim addresses losses and other remedies available under the applicable law. [U.S. Courts guide to civil cases](https://www.uscourts.gov/about-federal-courts/types-cases/civil-cases)

## Keep the criminal and civil records separate

Write down the crash report number, the investigating agency, and any criminal case number. Check whether a document is an initial crash report, a citation, a laboratory result, or the final court disposition. An arrest, a test result, and a conviction are different events. If timing matters, note when the collision happened, when an officer observed the driver, and when a sample was collected. [NHTSA overview of alcohol-impaired driving](https://www.nhtsa.gov/risky-driving/drunk-driving)

Look for evidence of the collision itself. The point of impact, witness vantage points, signal timing, and original video can bear on who caused which part of the crash. If a witness saw a vehicle cross the center line, record the witness's words and where they were standing. Ask a business or agency about preserving relevant footage before it is routinely overwritten. The [Claim Evidence Organizer](/tools/evidence-to-fact-map) can keep each observation beside the record that supports it.

## Separate losses from questions about punitive damages

Start with ordinary loss records. Match medical charges to the explanation of benefits and payment history. Track missed work with pay records and a dated work restriction. Keep repair estimates and receipts for actual transportation expenses. Review [what goes into a car accident settlement](/articles/how-much-is-my-car-accident-settlement-worth-in-2025-complete-guide) before comparing offers with different terms. [CMS guide to reading an explanation of benefits](https://www.cms.gov/initiatives/your-patient-rights/medical-bill-rights/get-help/guides-resources/read-explanation-benefits)

Punitive damages depend on the jurisdiction, what the evidence shows, and applicable coverage. Florida provides a concrete example. Its intoxication provision makes two specified punitive-damages provisions inapplicable to a defendant meeting its impairment or alcohol-level conditions at the time of the act or omission. Whether a claimant can obtain punitive damages still requires analysis of the case. [Florida Statutes § 768.736](https://flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2026/768.736)

## Compare the written terms of an offer

Ask what policies and limits the adjuster evaluated, what the payment would resolve, and who would sign the release. A bodily injury release can have different consequences from a payment for vehicle damage. A criminal restitution order, if one exists, also deserves its own entry so that the same expense is accounted for accurately.

Keep an offer's gross amount, costs, and any repayment claim on separate lines. The [Net Settlement Calculator](/tools/settlement-net-waterfall) shows the arithmetic under the figures you enter. The [guide to settlement versus trial](/articles/settlement-vs-trial-which-path-to-choose-for-your-personal-injury-case-in-2026) explains what to check alongside the number, including the scope of a release and the evidence still in dispute.

title: What to Bring to a First Personal Injury Lawyer Consultation
content:
Confirm how long the meeting will last, who will attend, and whether it is free or has a charge. A certified referral service can help locate a lawyer by practice area. The State Bar of California describes how certified referral services work and provides a directory for that state. Check the lawyer's license and public disciplinary information with the regulator in the relevant jurisdiction. [State Bar of California referral service directory](https://www.calbar.ca.gov/public/find-legal-professionals/find-lawyer-referral-service)

## Bring the documents that answer the first questions

Prepare a one-page chronology with dates and sources. Include the incident, first medical evaluation, insurance notices, and current status. Bring the report number, relevant policy or written denial, signed agreements, and any written deadline. List records you are still waiting for. The [Insurance Claim Timeline Builder](/tools/claim-timeline-builder) can sort the events without requiring you to share the entries online.

Ask how to provide records securely and whether the lawyer needs to check for conflicts before reviewing a full file. Redact unrelated identifiers from copies for an initial discussion when appropriate. Keep originals and label any redacted copy.

## Ask what is being evaluated

- Which claims, parties, or coverage questions appear relevant?
- What facts or documents would change that assessment?
- Which deadline needs immediate verification, and who will handle it?
- Who would work on the case and communicate updates?
- What work would start only after a representation agreement is signed?

A notice deadline for a public defendant can differ from an ordinary filing deadline. Take any government correspondence or incident report to the meeting and ask for the rule that applies. [California Courts guide to government claims](https://selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/civil-lawsuit/government-claim) · [Guide to checking filing deadlines](/articles/statute-of-limitations-for-personal-injury-claims-a-complete-2026-guide-by-state)

## Review the fee agreement line by line

Ask how a contingency fee is calculated, whether litigation expenses are taken before or after the percentage, and who owes expenses if the case ends without a recovery. Ask whether the percentage changes with filing, trial, or appeal and what the agreement covers. The California State Bar distinguishes attorney fees from costs and explains common billing arrangements. Read the written agreement for your case. [State Bar guidance on fees and billing](https://www.calbar.ca.gov/public/legal-resources/working-attorney/what-expect-regarding-fees-and-billing)

Bring a written offer if you have one. The [Net Settlement Calculator](/tools/settlement-net-waterfall) can compare alternative fee bases and deductions after the lawyer explains the actual terms. For situations that may need prompt legal review, see [when to speak with a personal injury lawyer](/articles/when-should-you-hire-a-personal-injury-attorney-9-signs-you-need-one-now).

title: Catastrophic Injury Claims: Documenting Long-Term Care Costs
content:
A useful long-term cost estimate begins with a service and a reason. For example, a written therapy recommendation can establish the expected frequency, while a provider estimate can supply the unit price. Keep the recommendation, price, and assumed duration in separate columns. California's civil jury instruction on medical expenses offers one example of the distinction between past reasonable costs and future care reasonably certain to be needed. [California Civil Jury Instructions, CACI 3903A](https://courts.ca.gov/system/files/file/judicial_council_of_california_civil_jury_instructions_2026.pdf#page=2706)

## Separate present care from future needs

Group records into care already received, care recommended for a defined period, and needs that require further evaluation. Include the source and date for each entry. For home support, describe the task, hours per week, and what changed after the injury. For equipment, record the model, quote, expected maintenance, and the reason behind any replacement interval.

Future care after a serious brain injury can involve several disciplines, including rehabilitation and therapy matched to the person's needs. A clinician can describe the function or goal each service addresses. The [brain injury record guide](/articles/brain-injury-compensation-in-2026-understanding-long-term-costs-and-settlement-values) explains how to keep symptoms, rehabilitation, and work restrictions linked to specific dates. [NINDS overview of traumatic brain injury and rehabilitation](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/sites/default/files/2025-07/NINDS_TBI_Booklet_Digital_508c.pdf)

## Show the assumptions behind a low and high scenario

Suppose a written plan calls for two visits per week for 12 weeks. If two estimates are $120 and $155 per visit, the illustrative range is $2,880 to $3,720 for 24 visits. Record whether the quotes include evaluations or equipment. If the frequency changes after reassessment, update that assumption in its own row. The [Medical Care Cost Planner](/tools/care-cost-scenario-planner) compares unit prices and quantities, and the [Household Help Cost Calculator](/tools/household-help-cost-planner) converts weekly hours and rates into a separate subtotal.

Some costs may recur monthly and others only when equipment is replaced. Track timing before combining them. Add a source for every price and label which items still need confirmation. A long-term projection may require clinical, vocational, and financial evidence appropriate to the case.

## Reconcile billed charges, balances, and future projections

For completed care, match bills with the corresponding EOB and payments. For proposed care, keep the quote and plan's coverage terms separate from actual out-of-pocket spending. A conditional payment or a reimbursement claim can affect how proceeds are distributed after a settlement. Keep that amount outside the projected care subtotal until you know what it represents. [CMS guide to reading a medical bill](https://www.cms.gov/initiatives/your-patient-rights/medical-bill-rights/get-help/guides-resources/how-read-your-bill) · [CMS beneficiary recovery process](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/coordination-benefits-recovery/beneficiary-services/recovery-process)

Maintain separate worksheets for care, [lost wages and earning capacity](/articles/lost-wages-claims-how-to-calculate-and-maximize-your-compensation-in-2026), and changes in daily function. A structured record makes it easier to see whether one service appears in two categories, whether a quote is out of date, or whether you still need a written recommendation.

title: Pedestrian Accident Claims: What to Do and What to Document
content:
After a vehicle strikes a pedestrian, immediate safety comes first. Call 911 for injuries or immediate danger. Get to a safe place if you can do so safely and follow emergency responders' instructions. Ask someone else to record the vehicle or witness details if you need care. [NHTSA pedestrian safety guidance](https://www.nhtsa.gov/road-safety/pedestrian-safety) · [California Department of Insurance crash guide](https://www.insurance.ca.gov/01-consumers/105-type/95-guides/01-auto/hadaccident.cfm)

## Record the crossing as it was that day

An intersection name alone rarely tells the story. Record the side of the street, direction of travel, location of the impact, lane markings, nearby signals, and any sight obstruction. At dusk or night, note working streetlights and lighting conditions. If a witness saw the signal change, record what they observed and from where. A later photo of the intersection can explain the layout. Keep the date of the photo so a reader can distinguish it from the original scene.

Write down the police report number and the names of any businesses or transit operators with cameras in view. Video may have a short retention period. A written preservation request can identify a time window, location, and camera direction. Keep a copy of the request and any response. Use the [Accident Photo Checklist](/tools/photo-documentation-planner) and [Insurance Claim Timeline Builder](/tools/claim-timeline-builder) to organize material you already have.

When the crossing indication is disputed, request the plan for the exact crosswalk and any available event logs for the incident. [How to request crosswalk signal timing records](/articles/crosswalk-signal-timing-records-pedestrian-crash).

## Work out whose conduct and whose coverage are in question

The driver's turn, speed, lookout, and signal use can matter. The pedestrian's route and signal phase may also matter under the applicable rules. NHTSA describes safety responsibilities for both drivers and people walking. State law supplies the duties and rules used in an individual claim. Where a public agency's design or maintenance may be involved, check promptly for a separate government claim procedure. California's courts, for example, explain that many personal injury claims against a government agency require an initial claim within six months. [California Courts guide to government claims](https://selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/civil-lawsuit/government-claim)

Keep a coverage list as well as a fault list. Ask whether the driver's liability policy, a work-vehicle policy, or coverage available to the injured person may apply. A person walking can have auto-policy questions about insured status and the circumstances of the collision. Ask the insurer to point to the relevant policy provisions in writing. If the driver left the scene, see the [hit-and-run coverage guide](/articles/hit-and-run-accident-what-to-do-who-pays-and-how-to-protect-your-rights-in-2026). [California Department of Insurance auto coverage guide](https://www.insurance.ca.gov/01-consumers/105-type/95-guides/01-auto/auto101.cfm)

## Document how the injury affected the days after the crash

Keep the first medical evaluation and the follow-up instructions. Save the date and source of work restrictions, any documented change in duties, and the costs you actually incurred. Compare a medical bill with the insurer's explanation of benefits for the same service before treating the amount on the bill as your remaining balance. [CMS guide to comparing a bill and an EOB](https://www.cms.gov/initiatives/your-patient-rights/medical-bill-rights/get-help/guides-resources/how-read-your-bill)

The [lost wages guide](/articles/lost-wages-claims-how-to-calculate-and-maximize-your-compensation-in-2026) explains how to turn schedules and pay records into an estimate someone else can check. If recovery affects a daily task such as stairs or walking to a bus stop, the [Daily Activity Recovery Journal](/tools/daily-function-journal) can record the change over time.

title: Insurance Bad Faith: How to Document Claim Handling
content:
A disagreement about the amount or coverage can require a close reading of the policy. A claim-handling concern raises additional questions about what the insurer knew, what it did, and when. State law determines the applicable duties, available remedies, and procedures. California's insurance department publishes claim-handling rules as one example. [California fair claims settlement regulations](https://www.insurance.ca.gov/01-consumers/130-laws-regs-hearings/05-CCR/fair-claims-regs.cfm)

## Identify the relationship and the issue

Start with the coverage and the parties. A first-party claim seeks benefits under coverage available to the claimant. A liability claim can involve an insurer's handling of a demand against its insured. Different obligations and procedures can apply. Record whose policy it is, which benefit or demand is in dispute, and which documents the insurer relied on. [California auto insurance coverage guide](https://www.insurance.ca.gov/01-consumers/105-type/95-guides/01-auto/auto101.cfm)

For a disputed delay, record when notice and supporting documents reached the insurer, what it asked for, and what response you received. For a disputed valuation, preserve the report, comparables, and any written reasons for adjustments. A missing document, an unexplained change of position, and a coverage disagreement each need a different question.

## Use the timeline to test a specific allegation

Create one entry per communication. Include the sender, date received, attachment list, and response date. Use the [Insurance Claim Contact Log](/tools/claim-contact-ledger) and keep delivery proof with your documents. A short example: if the insurer says it still needs the July repair estimate, identify which version it requested, when you sent it, and the message confirming receipt. That record is more useful than saying the insurer delayed.

The [Harvey case](/articles/why-a-policy-limits-check-did-not-end-this-bad-faith-case) shows why a missing communication can matter even where a carrier tenders limits. The Florida decision addresses an older record. Florida's current statute provides a conditional tender rule for liability insurance bad-faith claims. The 90-day period in subsection (4) depends on actual notice with evidence sufficient to support the claim amount, and on tender of the lesser of the limits or amount demanded. Separate notice requirements can apply under subsection (3). [Florida Statutes § 624.155](https://flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2026/624.155)

## Match the next step to the problem

Ask for a written decision and the documents or policy provisions behind it. If you believe the insurer's conduct violates state requirements, the state insurance department can review a consumer complaint within its role. Preserve the underlying appeal or filing dates independently. The [Insurance Complaint Organizer](/tools/insurance-complaint-packet) helps assemble a factual timeline, supporting records, and requested outcome. [NAIC guide to filing a complaint](https://content.naic.org/consumer/how-to-file-complaint)

If the first issue is a written denial, follow the [coverage denial and bad-faith guide](/articles/bad-faith-insurance-what-to-do-when-your-insurance-company-refuses-to-pay-in-2026) to separate the policy question from the way the claim was handled.

title: Premises Liability: Who Controlled the Property and the Hazard?
content:
A property injury can raise questions about ownership, control, maintenance, and notice. The owner, tenant, property manager, or contractor may have had different responsibilities. Start with the exact location and the task that could have prevented the injury. California's premises instructions, for example, ask about ownership or control, reasonable care, harm, and causation. The applicable state's rules determine the elements for a particular claim. [California Civil Jury Instructions, CACI 1000 and 1001](https://courts.ca.gov/system/files/file/judicial_council_of_california_civil_jury_instructions_2026.pdf#page=700)

## Identify who controlled the specific area

Describe the area precisely. “North entrance, outside the automatic doors” is more useful than the name of a shopping center. Ask who inspected the area, who could make a repair or put up a warning, and whether the tenant or a common-area manager was responsible. A deed, lease, work order, or service contract can point to different people. A name on a sign alone does not explain control of that area.

The law may consider why someone was on the property, whether the condition was open and obvious, and what reasonable care required under the circumstances. A single national chart of visitor categories can obscure important state differences. California's instructions illustrate a duty analysis focused on the circumstances. [California Civil Jury Instructions, premises liability series](https://courts.ca.gov/system/files/file/judicial_council_of_california_civil_jury_instructions_2026.pdf#page=700)

## Connect the condition to notice and the injury

Photograph the condition and its surroundings when it is safe. Include measurements or context where relevant. Record who observed the hazard, whether anyone reported it before the incident, and what the inspection or repair records say. For a recurring leak, earlier work orders or repeated complaints can address a different question from a photo taken after a fall.

Florida's statute for a slip on a transitory foreign substance in a business establishment specifically addresses actual or constructive knowledge. Other premises claims can turn on different duties and evidence. See the [slip-and-fall evidence guide](/articles/slip-and-fall-accidents-whos-liable-and-what-your-case-is-worth-in-2026) for a worked example of what can establish notice in that setting. [Florida Statutes § 768.0755](https://flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2026/768.0755)

If an animal caused the injury, keep the animal owner's conduct separate from any question about who controlled a gate, fence, or common area. The [dog bite guide](/articles/dog-bite-laws-in-2026-your-complete-guide-to-victim-rights-and-compensation) compares the state rules that can govern the animal owner's liability.

## Organize what you know and what remains open

Make a list of the condition, who controlled it, what the relevant parties knew, how the injury happened, and what supports each fact. The [Claim Evidence Organizer](/tools/evidence-to-fact-map) can keep records and open questions side by side. A photo may show a broken tread. An inspection schedule may show who should have checked it. Neither substitutes for a record connecting the condition to the injury.

If a public entity controls the site, check the [filing and notice deadline guide](/articles/statute-of-limitations-for-personal-injury-claims-a-complete-2026-guide-by-state) early. Some jurisdictions require a government claim before a lawsuit. California's self-help court guide describes the separate claim procedure and timing. [California Courts government claim guidance](https://selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/civil-lawsuit/government-claim)

title: Lost Wages After an Injury: How to Calculate and Document Them
content:
A lost-wage worksheet should explain which work you missed, how you know it was scheduled, and how much you were actually paid for that period. Past missed pay and reduced future earning capacity are separate questions. California's civil jury instructions address them separately in CACI 3903C and 3903D. The law and evidence requirements in an individual case may differ. [California Civil Jury Instructions](https://courts.ca.gov/system/files/file/judicial_council_of_california_civil_jury_instructions_2026.pdf#page=2713)

## Reconcile the schedule with the pay stub

Start with the affected dates and duties. Use a timecard, shift roster, or appointment book for the expected work. Add the clinician's work restrictions or a dated employer note describing the change in schedule. Compare what you would have worked with what the employer actually paid, including any replacement shifts or paid hours. The U.S. Department of Labor's recordkeeping guidance lists records covered employers generally maintain for nonexempt employees. [DOL wage and hour recordkeeping guidance](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fact-sheets/21-flsa-recordkeeping?lang=en)

- **Hourly work.** Separate regular hours from documented overtime. The federal overtime rule generally applies after 40 hours in a workweek for covered, nonexempt workers. Use the pay terms and applicable rules for your own job. [DOL overtime guidance](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/overtime)
- **Salary.** Determine which pay periods actually changed. Use the employer's pay basis and any payroll deductions or reductions. A daily rate is useful as a planning estimate when its annual workday assumption is explicit.
- **Variable pay or self-employment.** Compare periods of similar length and workload. Separate gross receipts from business expenses and keep the reason for each comparison visible. Cancellations, invoices, deposits, and tax records may help substantiate a claim.

## Work through the arithmetic before adding deductions

For example, assume a worker missed 32 documented unpaid regular hours at $24 per hour and four unpaid hours that would have been paid at $36 per hour. The gross scenario is $768 plus $144, or $912. If eight of the regular hours were paid through leave, move those hours to a separate leave column and recalculate unpaid wages. The status of used leave as a claimed loss depends on the applicable rules and facts.

Enter your own rates and hours in the [Hourly Lost Wages Calculator](/tools/hourly-lost-work-calculator). Use the [Paid Leave and Unpaid Time Calculator](/tools/paid-leave-splitter) to track different types of time, or the [Gig Worker Income Loss Calculator](/tools/gig-net-income-comparison) to compare net results for matching periods.

## Record reduced work capacity separately

A future claim may depend on more than current hours missed. Keep written restrictions, duration estimates, job duties, and records of changes in assignments or opportunities. Separate a clinician's work restriction from a financial projection of its effect. CACI 3903D offers one jurisdiction-specific example of how loss of earning capacity is framed. [California Civil Jury Instructions](https://courts.ca.gov/system/files/file/judicial_council_of_california_civil_jury_instructions_2026.pdf#page=2715)

If you were injured at work, see [how workers' compensation handles work restrictions and wage benefits](/articles/workers-compensation-in-2026-the-complete-guide-to-your-rights-after-a-workplace-injury). For an injury settlement, put the wage worksheet alongside medical, property, and other expense records using the [car accident settlement breakdown](/articles/how-much-is-my-car-accident-settlement-worth-in-2025-complete-guide).

title: Personal Injury Settlement Timeline: What Can Move a Case Forward?
content:
Two injury claims can begin on the same date and move at very different speeds. One may involve an undisputed policy and complete records. Another may need additional treatment evidence, multiple insurers, or a court ruling before the parties can evaluate an offer. Track the events that actually happened and the specific records or decisions still pending. [U.S. Courts overview of the civil case process](https://www.uscourts.gov/about-federal-courts/types-cases/civil-cases)

## Keep three timelines in the same file

- **Care and work.** Record appointments, changes in treatment, restrictions, and dates when the clinician expects to reassess. Keep the expected dates distinct from visits that already occurred.
- **Claim correspondence.** Record notice, requests for records, submissions, written decisions, and offers. Save the exact documents and any proof of delivery. [NAIC auto claim documentation guide](https://content.naic.org/article/what-you-should-know-about-filing-auto-claim)
- **Legal and policy dates.** Write down any filing, notice, appeal, or contract deadlines with their source. Negotiations and medical treatment can continue while a deadline approaches. Read the [limitations guide](/articles/statute-of-limitations-for-personal-injury-claims-a-complete-2026-guide-by-state) for examples of different clocks. [California Courts explanation of lawsuit deadlines](https://selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/civil-lawsuit/statute-limitations)

The [Insurance Claim Timeline Builder](/tools/claim-timeline-builder) sorts dated events while keeping the evidence attached. Use the [Insurance Claim Date and Reminder Planner](/tools/important-date-planner) for dates you have independently confirmed.

## Identify what is preventing the next decision

An insurer may be waiting for a specific item, such as a repair estimate, a medical record for one date, or clarification about which policy applied. Ask in writing what remains outstanding and what action comes next. Keep a dated copy of the request and response. If an adjuster says a claim is under review, ask which issue is being reviewed and whether any document is missing.

A potential settlement has its own steps. Review the offer, scope of release, parties who must sign, expected payment terms, and unresolved deductions. If a repayment demand is pending, record its stage. The [Medicare recovery case](/articles/a-125000-crash-settlement-and-medicares-repayment-demand) explains why a conditional-payment list and a final demand can arrive at different points in the process. [CMS beneficiary recovery process](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/coordination-benefits-recovery/beneficiary-services/recovery-process)

## Understand what filing adds to the timeline

Litigation may add service, scheduling orders, discovery, motions, mediation, and trial. Discovery can include document requests and testimony. In federal civil cases, the court describes several opportunities for parties to resolve disputes before trial. Procedures depend on the forum and case. [U.S. Courts civil cases overview](https://www.uscourts.gov/about-federal-courts/types-cases/civil-cases) · [California Courts civil discovery guide](https://selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/discovery-civil/request)

For planning, write the next event as a task you can verify. For example, “Confirm receipt of the orthopedic report by Friday” is useful. “The insurer should settle next month” gives you no record to follow. See the [settlement versus trial guide](/articles/settlement-vs-trial-which-path-to-choose-for-your-personal-injury-case-in-2026) for the decision points that a timeline alone cannot answer.

title: Construction Injuries: Workers’ Compensation and Third-Party Claims
content:
One site can have a general contractor, subcontractors, an equipment supplier, and a property owner. Record who employed the injured worker, who directed the task, and who provided or controlled the equipment involved. The workers' compensation question starts with the employment and work injury. A separate civil question may concern the conduct of another entity and what caused the injury. [California DWC injured worker guidebook](https://www.dir.ca.gov/InjuredWorkerGuidebook/InjuredWorkerGuidebook.html)

## Keep two records of the same incident

For workers' compensation, document when you reported the injury, the claim form, medical treatment, and restrictions. State rules govern coverage and benefits. For a possible third-party claim, preserve the task assignment, equipment identification, witness accounts, inspection records, and the role of each business. California Labor Code § 3852 is one example of a statute that allows an employee to pursue a claim against a person other than the employer while also claiming workers' compensation, subject to applicable rules. [California Supreme Court discussion of Labor Code § 3852](https://www.courts.ca.gov/opinions/archive/S232197.PDF) · [U.S. Department of Labor state agency directory](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/owcp/wc)

Use separate columns for employer, site supervisor, equipment owner, and witness. If a rented lift was involved, record the serial number, who inspected it, and the time of the last service. A service record can help identify what the supplier did. A daily work order may address who controlled the task.

## Use safety standards to ask precise questions

OSHA's construction focus materials address falls, struck-by incidents, caught-in or between hazards, and electrocution. Federal construction fall-protection rules set requirements for different conditions and tasks. Identify the work surface, height, task, and protective system in use before applying a provision. A safety standard can help identify relevant evidence. Who owed a duty and whether a condition caused an injury are separate questions under the applicable law. [OSHA Construction Focus Four](https://www.osha.gov/training/outreach/construction/focus-four) · [OSHA fall protection standard, 29 C.F.R. § 1926.501](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1926/1926.501)

The [Claim Evidence Organizer](/tools/evidence-to-fact-map) can match each issue to a record. The [Accident Photo Checklist](/tools/photo-documentation-planner) can help group existing photos by location and equipment. Follow site safety rules and preserve originals through an appropriate process.

## Track benefits and payments without duplicating an expense

Keep medical payments, wage replacement, actual missed pay, and any third-party recovery separate. Where both a benefits claim and another claim exist, reimbursement or credit issues may affect the final distribution under state law. Confirm how each payment will be handled before accepting settlement terms. Review the [workers’ compensation guide](/articles/workers-compensation-in-2026-the-complete-guide-to-your-rights-after-a-workplace-injury) for filing and care questions and the [settlement comparison guide](/articles/settlement-vs-trial-which-path-to-choose-for-your-personal-injury-case-in-2026) for a written offer. [California regulation on workers’ compensation credit petitions](https://www.dir.ca.gov/t8/10555.html)

title: Settlement vs. Trial: Compare the Terms, Costs, and Risks
content:
A settlement is an agreement on terms. A trial asks a judge or jury to resolve issues the parties have not resolved. Settlement discussions can occur before or during litigation, and mediation may help the parties explore an agreement. The U.S. Courts civil case guide describes discovery and trial as distinct stages, with opportunities to resolve the dispute along the way. [U.S. Courts overview of civil cases](https://www.uscourts.gov/about-federal-courts/types-cases/civil-cases)

## Review the offer as a document

Ask for the proposed agreement and payment terms. Identify who pays, who is released, which claims are covered, and when payment is due. Check whether the offer separates property and injury claims, and what happens to outstanding bills or asserted repayment rights. Ask how the fee agreement handles case expenses and the basis for calculating the fee. [California State Bar guidance on fees and costs](https://www.calbar.ca.gov/public/legal-resources/working-attorney/what-expect-regarding-fees-and-billing)

Use the [Compare Net Settlement Offers tool](/tools/offer-net-comparison) for the numbers. In an illustrative example, a $30,000 offer with $8,000 in combined deductions leaves $22,000. A $32,000 offer with $12,000 in deductions leaves $20,000. The better comparison still depends on the release, timing, certainty of payment, and whether each deduction is supported. If Medicare is involved, see [how its recovery process can affect settlement proceeds](/articles/a-125000-crash-settlement-and-medicares-repayment-demand). [CMS beneficiary recovery process](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/coordination-benefits-recovery/beneficiary-services/recovery-process)

## Make a list of what would have to be proved

For each disputed issue, write the evidence that supports your position and the evidence that cuts against it. Label what remains uncertain. A witness may explain what happened before the collision, while a clinician may address causation or treatment. The [Claim Evidence Organizer](/tools/evidence-to-fact-map) helps keep those questions distinct.

Trial preparation can involve experts, depositions, document exchanges, and motions. A verdict may still be followed by post-trial proceedings or an appeal, and collection can be a separate practical issue. Ask counsel how fees, expenses, appeals, and collection would be handled under your actual agreement. [U.S. Courts overview of civil proceedings](https://www.uscourts.gov/about-federal-courts/types-cases/civil-cases)

## Compare scenarios without turning them into predictions

A hypothetical favorable and unfavorable outcome can make the assumptions visible. The [Break-Even Probability Calculator](/tools/outcome-break-even-sandbox) compares arithmetic scenarios you enter. It supplies no probability for the dispute. A decision can also turn on factors that fit poorly into one dollar amount, such as uncertain timing or whether the release covers a separate claim.

Keep the [settlement timeline guide](/articles/personal-injury-settlement-timeline-how-long-does-it-really-take-in-2026) next to the written offer. Review the next procedural deadline separately from how long the offer remains open. A deadline for accepting an offer and a deadline for filing a claim can have different sources and consequences. [California Courts guide to filing deadlines](https://selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/civil-lawsuit/statute-limitations)

title: Talking to an Insurance Adjuster After a Crash
content:
Before an adjuster call, confirm the company, claim number, and coverage under review. Your own insurer may ask for information under the policy's notice and cooperation provisions. A request from another party's insurer may raise different questions. Ask what is required, under which policy or procedure, and by when. Keep any deadline in writing. [California Department of Insurance auto claims guide](https://www.insurance.ca.gov/01-consumers/105-type/95-guides/01-auto/hadaccident.cfm)

## Use direct answers and keep uncertainty visible

Provide the basic facts you know, such as the date, location, vehicles, and report number. When you do not remember a detail, say so. For example, “I saw the vehicle enter the intersection. I don't know its speed.” A photograph or video may later supply more information. Keep the first account and any correction with their own dates. [NAIC auto claim documentation guidance](https://content.naic.org/article/what-you-should-know-about-filing-auto-claim)

If asked how you are doing, describe current observations accurately and distinguish them from medical conclusions. “My evaluation is scheduled for Tuesday” is more precise than guessing about diagnosis or recovery. Share relevant medical or employment records through the agreed claim process and keep a copy of what you sent.

## Clarify a request for a recorded statement or authorization

Ask who will record it, what issues it covers, whether a copy or transcript is available, and when a response is due. Ask for the policy basis if your insurer treats it as required. A broad authorization to obtain records may have a different scope from supplying a specific report or bill. Ask which providers, dates, and records the request covers. If there is a dispute about the scope or obligation, a local lawyer can explain the applicable terms and law. [California Department of Insurance guide to reporting a claim](https://www.insurance.ca.gov/01-consumers/105-type/95-guides/01-auto/hadaccident.cfm)

Use the [Compare Two Claim Statements tool](/tools/statement-version-comparator) to compare a transcript or summary with your notes. A difference may be a simple mistake or a point that needs clarification. Save both versions with the date and origin of each.

## Close the call with a checkable next step

Write down the requested document, who will send it, and any confirmed date. For example, ask “Can you confirm whether you need the itemized bill, the EOB, or both?” The [Insurance Claim Follow-Up Email Builder](/tools/claim-follow-up-composer) can turn that into a short message you can review before sending. [NAIC guidance on keeping claim correspondence](https://content.naic.org/article/what-you-should-know-about-filing-auto-claim)

If the adjuster mentions a “final offer,” ask for the amount, deadline, and proposed release in writing. See [five insurance requests worth clarifying](/articles/insurance-adjusters-5-dirty-tactics-they-use-against-you-and-how-to-fight-back) for document-by-document questions and the [denied claim guide](/articles/how-to-fight-a-denied-insurance-claim-and-win) if you receive a written adverse decision.

If the insurer says an upload is missing, [match your portal receipt to the adjuster's list of readable files](/articles/insurance-claim-portal-upload-missing). If it issues a different denial after reviewing the file, [compare the two reasons in writing](/articles/insurer-changed-denial-reason-complaint).

title: Hit-and-Run Accidents: Reporting, Evidence, and Coverage
content:
When the other driver leaves, the immediate tasks are safety and reporting. Call 911 if someone is injured or the scene poses a danger. If you can do so safely, record a partial plate, vehicle description, direction of travel, and time. Give those details to the responding agency and follow its instructions. [California Department of Insurance crash guide](https://www.insurance.ca.gov/01-consumers/105-type/95-guides/01-auto/hadaccident.cfm)

## Build an identification record

A plate fragment, a distinctive mark, and a timestamp may be more useful together than separately. Ask witnesses what they observed in their own words and keep their contact details private. Save original dashcam or phone files with the device's date and time information. If a business camera may have captured the event, record the camera's location and ask promptly about preservation. Keep later copies and edits separate from originals. If someone walking was struck, see the [pedestrian crash evidence guide](/articles/pedestrian-accident-rights-2026-what-to-do-if-youre-hit-by-a-vehicle) for how to record the crossing and signal phase.

Report the event to the insurer as required by the policy. Record the report number, the agency, and the name of each person you contacted. Note if the officer prepared an incident report or if another agency is handling the investigation. The [Insurance Claim Contact Log](/tools/claim-contact-ledger) keeps the police record, claim number, and follow-up dates distinct. [NAIC auto claim guide](https://content.naic.org/article/what-you-should-know-about-filing-auto-claim)

If a tow ticket is your earliest record, use its pickup details to identify the operator, first lot and possible corroborating sources. [How to document a hit-and-run without scene photos](/articles/hit-and-run-claim-tow-receipt-no-scene-photos).

## Review coverage by type of loss

Vehicle repairs and injuries may follow different routes. Collision coverage can apply to covered damage to your own vehicle, subject to the policy terms and deductible. Uninsured motorist bodily injury coverage is a separate question. Ask whether the definition of an uninsured or unidentified vehicle applies, what proof the policy requires, and whether notice or contact requirements apply where you live. California's consumer guide distinguishes uninsured motorist bodily injury from uninsured motorist property damage and explains that its property-damage coverage has identification restrictions. [California auto insurance coverage guide](https://www.insurance.ca.gov/01-consumers/105-type/95-guides/01-auto/auto101.cfm)

Request the declarations page and any endorsements that affect the loss. Write down each coverage's deductible and limit in a separate column. An adjuster's first answer may address only one coverage. If the insurer says the vehicle must be identified, ask which coverage that statement applies to and where the requirement appears in the policy. The [guide to a denied claim](/articles/how-to-fight-a-denied-insurance-claim-and-win) shows how to turn that answer into a focused written request.

## Keep transport expenses tied to dates

If you need a rental while a vehicle is inspected or repaired, ask what the policy covers per day, how long coverage lasts, and whether there is a total cap. Save the authorization, rental agreement, and return receipt. If your policy allows $35 per day for an eligible rental costing $50 per day, the daily gap is $15 before other terms, taxes, or limits. Use the [Rental Car Coverage Gap Calculator](/tools/rental-budget-stress-test) with your written terms.

A hit-and-run claim still benefits from the same record of injuries and expenses as other collisions. The [post-crash checklist](/articles/what-to-do-after-a-car-accident-a-complete-step-by-step-guide) and [car settlement breakdown](/articles/how-much-is-my-car-accident-settlement-worth-in-2025-complete-guide) cover the next records to collect.

title: Brain Injury Claims: Care, Work, and Daily Function
content:
Traumatic brain injury can affect memory, concentration, balance, sleep, mood, and other functions. After a head injury, get medical guidance about new symptoms. CDC lists danger signs requiring immediate emergency care, including repeated vomiting, seizures, or a headache that worsens and does not go away. Symptoms can emerge later. The clinical record and follow-up matter for care. [CDC concussion symptoms and danger signs](https://www.cdc.gov/traumatic-brain-injury/signs-symptoms/index.html)

## Record change over time using specific tasks

Start a timeline with the injury, first evaluation, follow-up visits, and documented changes in symptoms or function. Use the provider's wording for diagnoses and restrictions. For observations at home, write down the task, what happened, and whether assistance or extra time was needed. Someone who previously managed a weekly grocery trip alone, for example, might now use a list, require a ride, or need a break partway through. The [Daily Activity Recovery Journal](/tools/daily-function-journal) can organize comparable entries.

Rehabilitation can address different needs. Speech-language, occupational, physical, or other therapies may be recommended depending on the injury. Record who recommended each service, the treatment goal, and the date of reassessment. [NINDS traumatic brain injury overview](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/sites/default/files/2025-07/NINDS_TBI_Booklet_Digital_508c.pdf)

## Connect work restrictions to actual earnings and tasks

A return-to-work plan may describe shorter shifts, rest breaks, or changes in duties. Compare the written plan with actual hours and pay across the same dates. A dated work schedule and pay statement can help show when the change affected earnings. The [Return-to-Work Hours and Pay Calculator](/tools/phased-return-work-planner) compares baseline and actual hours under an entered rate. A claim about future capacity needs a separate assessment. [CDC guidance on returning to activities after a mild TBI](https://www.cdc.gov/heads-up/hcp/clinical-guidance/) · [Lost wages documentation guide](/articles/lost-wages-claims-how-to-calculate-and-maximize-your-compensation-in-2026)

## Keep the care estimate separate from the injury narrative

A service log can show what rehabilitation took place. A budget can show what an expected future course might cost. The two should use different source columns. For care already received, verify itemized charges against the plan's explanation and actual payments. For care that may be needed, use the provider's recommendation and quote or rate source. [CMS explanation of benefits guide](https://www.cms.gov/initiatives/your-patient-rights/medical-bill-rights/get-help/guides-resources/read-explanation-benefits)

The [long-term care cost guide](/articles/catastrophic-injury-compensation-2026-calculating-long-term-costs-and-maximum-recovery) shows how to document frequency, price, duration, and replacement assumptions. If the same difficulty is relevant to daily life as well as work, keep those effects distinct. For example, reduced paid work hours belong in a wage record, while the need for help with meals belongs in a daily-function or support record.

title: Wrongful Death Claims: Who Can File and What to Document
content:
After a death, relatives may receive requests from insurers, medical providers, or agencies before anyone has established who may act for the estate. Keep those requests, the relevant policies, and any appointment papers together. Eligibility to receive a share of a recovery and authority to file the claim can be different questions. New York's wrongful death statute illustrates that distinction by giving the right to maintain an action to a duly appointed personal representative in the circumstances it describes. [New York EPTL § 5-4.1](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/EPT/5-4.1)

## Identify the type of claim and the person who may act

A wrongful death action may address losses suffered by eligible beneficiaries. A separate survival provision can allow a claim that belonged to the decedent to continue through the estate. Each state's law determines who acts, who may benefit, and which damages are available. New York has separate provisions for wrongful death and the survival of certain causes of action. [New York EPTL §§ 5-4.1](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/EPT/5-4.1) and [11-3.2](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/EPT/11-3.2)

For the person reviewing the file, collect the death certificate when available, documents identifying any appointed representative, and the underlying incident record. If the death followed a hospital stay, ask counsel who may request the medical records and what proof of authority is required. HHS describes how a personal representative's authority relates to access under HIPAA. [HHS guidance on personal representatives](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/privacy/guidance/personal-representatives/index.html)

## Organize losses under the applicable rule

List each claimed loss with the document that supports it. Income records, records of support, and invoices for medical or funeral costs can answer different questions. New York's damages provision addresses pecuniary injuries to eligible beneficiaries and specified expenses. Other jurisdictions define recoverable losses differently. Avoid applying a general settlement range to a family or assuming every form of loss is recoverable. [New York EPTL § 5-4.3](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/EPT/5-4.3)

For a recurring contribution, preserve the actual dates and amounts. For an expense, save the invoice and the record of payment separately. The [Claim Expense and Receipt Tracker](/tools/receipt-coverage-map) can help sort invoices, payments, and reimbursements under your own labels.

## Confirm each deadline independently

New York generally requires the wrongful death action within two years after death, subject to the statute's exceptions. Government defendants can involve an additional notice requirement. New York's municipal notice statute includes a specific rule for the timing of notice in wrongful death actions. Verify both the responsible entity and the triggering date before relying on either period. [New York EPTL § 5-4.1](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/EPT/5-4.1) · [New York General Municipal Law § 50-e](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/GMU/50-E)

Use the [filing deadlines guide](/articles/statute-of-limitations-for-personal-injury-claims-a-complete-2026-guide-by-state) to distinguish notice from suit. If a consultation is next, the [first attorney consultation guide](/articles/free-case-evaluation-what-to-expect-from-your-first-attorney-consultation-in-2026) gives a way to organize the records and the questions about representation, fees, and next dates.

title: When an Insurance Denial Raises a Bad Faith Question
content:
Start with the exact reason the insurer gave. A policy exclusion, an expired policy, a missing record, and a dispute about who caused a loss are different reasons for a denial. Ask for the provision and facts the insurer relied on. Keep the policy version, declarations, endorsements, and denial together. [California Department of Insurance fair claims settlement regulations](https://www.insurance.ca.gov/01-consumers/130-laws-regs-hearings/05-CCR/fair-claims-regs.cfm)

## Read one reason against one policy provision

Make a table with the insurer's reason, relevant clause, document the insurer relied on, and your question. If the letter says a vehicle was used for work, ask which endorsement or exclusion applies to that vehicle, person, and trip. The [Pennsylvania work-car coverage case](/articles/can-your-auto-policy-cover-a-crash-in-a-work-car) illustrates why the precise policy wording and vehicle use can determine one coverage layer.

If the insurer says a document was missing, provide the record and transmission evidence if you have them. If you disagree with a condition adjustment or repair figure, request the report and identify the line you dispute. Use the [Insurance Claim Follow-Up Email Builder](/tools/claim-follow-up-composer) to draft a concise request with the claim reference and document dates. [NAIC auto claim guidance](https://content.naic.org/article/what-you-should-know-about-filing-auto-claim)

## Document how the insurer reached the decision

Record the first report, documents requested, submission dates, changes in explanation, and the final decision. A mistaken decision can be different from conduct that meets a state's bad-faith standard. Florida, for example, states that negligence alone is insufficient under its bad-faith statute and describes specific notice and tender provisions. A lawyer can evaluate whether the rule applies to the relationship and timing in your case. [Florida Statutes § 624.155](https://flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2026/624.155)

The [claim-handling timeline guide](/articles/how-to-deal-with-insurance-bad-faith-your-complete-2026-action-guide) shows how to preserve what each party knew and when. Focus the timeline on the decision in dispute. A letter dated March 2 may have been received on March 6. Keep both dates when the distinction matters.

## Keep review, complaints, and legal deadlines separate

Read the denial letter and applicable rules for reconsideration or appeal. A state insurance department can receive a complaint about insurer conduct. A complaint may serve a different purpose from challenging the benefit decision or filing a lawsuit. Save the complaint confirmation and track other deadlines by their own source. [NAIC consumer complaint guidance](https://content.naic.org/consumer/how-to-file-complaint)

For health-plan claims, the applicable internal appeal and independent external review procedures can differ from auto or property disputes. Review the [step-by-step denial guide](/articles/how-to-fight-a-denied-insurance-claim-and-win) for how to identify the correct process. [HealthCare.gov guide to internal appeals](https://www.healthcare.gov/appeal-insurance-company-decision/internal-appeals/)

title: Personal Injury Filing Deadlines: How to Check the Right Clock
content:
A statute of limitations gives a time limit for bringing a legal action. A government notice, insurance notice, health-plan appeal, and court filing can each have their own deadlines. Start by identifying the jurisdiction, claim, defendant, and the event that starts each clock. Filing requirements and exceptions can depend on facts such as when a claim accrued and which version of the law applies. [California Courts guide to filing deadlines](https://selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/civil-lawsuit/statute-limitations)

## Compare statutory examples before using a state number

- **California.** Many personal injury actions have a two-year limit. The courts describe separate periods for some claims, including medical malpractice. [California Courts deadline guide](https://selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/civil-lawsuit/statute-limitations)
- **Texas.** The general statute lists two years from accrual for personal injury. It separately addresses actions for injuries resulting in death. [Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code § 16.003](https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/CP/pdf/CP.16.pdf)
- **New York.** CPLR 214 generally lists three years for injury to person, subject to exceptions. Wrongful death has a separate statute. [New York CPLR 214](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/CVP/214) · [EPTL § 5-4.1](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/EPT/5-4.1)
- **Florida.** The current statute generally lists two years for actions founded on negligence. Verify which law applies to the date the claim accrued. [Florida Statutes § 95.11](https://m.flsenate.gov/Statutes/95.11)

These examples illustrate the need to match the claim to its rule. A bodily injury, medical malpractice, contract, or wrongful death claim may have a different period in the same state. Discovery, minority, statutes of repose, or special notice provisions can affect the analysis. Verify any exception with the actual statute and relevant facts. See the [medical malpractice records and deadlines guide](/articles/medical-malpractice-10-warning-signs-you-may-have-a-case-in-2026) and [wrongful death guide](/articles/wrongful-death-lawsuits-in-2026-a-familys-complete-guide-to-seeking-justice).

## Check public defendants separately

California courts explain that many injury claims against a government agency require submitting an initial claim within six months. New York's general municipal notice statute ordinarily requires notice within 90 days for covered tort claims, with specific provisions including the rule for wrongful death. Under the Federal Tort Claims Act, the statutory scheme generally includes presentment to the appropriate agency within two years of accrual and a six-month period after mailing of a final denial for bringing suit. Identify the agency and procedure before using any of these examples. [California government claim guide](https://selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/civil-lawsuit/government-claim) · [New York General Municipal Law § 50-e](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/GMU/50-E) · [28 U.S.C. §§ 2401](https://uscode.house.gov/us/usc/119-120/t28/s2401/) and [2675](https://uscode.house.gov/us/usc/119-134/t28/s2675/)

## Keep a record of confirmed dates and sources

Write down the injury date, dates of discovery or notice that may matter, which entity received any filing, and proof of delivery. For a confirmed deadline, include the rule or professional who confirmed it. The [Insurance Claim Date and Reminder Planner](/tools/important-date-planner) records dates you supply and exports them to a calendar. It supplies no legal deadline. The [settlement timeline guide](/articles/personal-injury-settlement-timeline-how-long-does-it-really-take-in-2026) explains how to keep negotiation milestones separate from formal filing and notice dates.

title: Dog Bite Claims: State Liability Rules and Records to Keep
content:
After a dog bite, address the injury and contact a medical professional or public health authority for guidance about infection and rabies risk. CDC advises washing an animal bite wound promptly and seeking appropriate medical attention based on the exposure and injury. Record the animal's identifying information and vaccination information if you can obtain it safely. Follow local reporting instructions. [CDC dog bite guidance](https://www.cdc.gov/healthy-pets/about/dogs.html) · [CDC rabies prevention guidance](https://www.cdc.gov/rabies/when-to-seek-care/)

## Compare two different legal approaches

California Civil Code § 3342 generally makes a dog owner liable for a bite in a public place or while the person is lawfully in a private place, subject to the statute's terms and exceptions. The California civil jury instruction identifies facts the claimant must establish, including ownership, bite, harm, and causation. The instruction does not require an earlier bite as a general element. [California Civil Jury Instructions, CACI 463](https://courts.ca.gov/system/files/file/judicial_council_of_california_civil_jury_instructions_2026.pdf#page=452)

New York's Court of Appeals addressed a different framework in *Flanders v. Goodfellow*. In 2025 it held that a claimant can rely on ordinary negligence for harm caused by a domestic animal. That route exists alongside strict liability when the owner knew or should have known of the animal's dangerous propensities. The decision allows a theory to be considered under its evidence. It supplies no outcome for another incident. [New York Court of Appeals opinion in Flanders](https://www.nycourts.gov/reporter/3dseries/2025/2025_02261.htm)

## Record the incident and the basis for each claim

Write down the location, who was handling the animal, why the injured person was there, and what witnesses observed. Save official animal-control or incident report references. If prior conduct matters, identify the source, date, and specific conduct instead of repeating a general description such as “the dog was aggressive.” If an incident involved a broken gate or a person holding a leash, note who controlled it. The [Claim Evidence Organizer](/tools/evidence-to-fact-map) can keep facts and supporting records together.

If the injury occurred at a business or rental property, the animal owner's conduct and another party's control of the premises are distinct questions. The [premises liability guide](/articles/premises-liability-law-explained-when-property-owners-are-responsible-in-2026) explains how to identify control and notice for a condition on the property.

When a dog reaches a delivery route through a gate, document who controlled the gate and how its latch worked on the relevant date. [What a gate latch can show in a New York delivery bite claim](/articles/new-york-dog-bite-delivery-gate-latch-evidence).

## Track treatment and related losses by date

Preserve medical records, itemized bills, payments, and documented time off. If treatment affected a specific task, note the date and how it changed. Make one list of costs already incurred and another of services a clinician has recommended. Check the [guide to filing and notice deadlines](/articles/statute-of-limitations-for-personal-injury-claims-a-complete-2026-guide-by-state) for why the claim type and state matter. [HHS right to access health records](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/what-personal-health-information-do-individuals/index.html) · [CMS medical bill guidance](https://www.cms.gov/initiatives/your-patient-rights/medical-bill-rights/get-help/guides-resources/how-read-your-bill)

title: Slip-and-Fall Claims: Hazard, Notice, and Evidence
content:
When you report a fall, identify the exact spot, time, surface, and condition. Ask how to obtain the incident report or its reference number. Document the scene if you can do so safely. Wide photographs can show the route and warnings. Close photographs can show the substance, tread, or change in elevation. Label the time and photographer so others can distinguish the incident from later conditions. [California Civil Jury Instructions, premises liability series](https://courts.ca.gov/system/files/file/judicial_council_of_california_civil_jury_instructions_2026.pdf#page=700)

## Identify the rule that fits the condition

A spill in a grocery aisle is different from a loose step, recurring leak, or broken railing. In Florida, the law for a transitory foreign substance in a business establishment requires evidence that the business had actual or constructive knowledge of the condition and should have acted. The statute gives two ways circumstantial evidence can establish constructive knowledge: the condition existed long enough for the business to have discovered it with ordinary care, or it recurred regularly enough to be foreseeable. [Florida Statutes § 768.0755](https://flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2026/768.0755)

For a fixed defect, maintenance requests, prior repairs, or inspection records may answer a different question about who was responsible and what they knew. See [the premises liability guide](/articles/premises-liability-law-explained-when-property-owners-are-responsible-in-2026) to identify the company or person with control of the specific area. Rules vary by state and type of property.

## Build a timeline around the condition

Suppose an illustrative store incident occurred at 3:10 p.m. A photograph at 3:13 p.m. can show what the floor looked like afterward. A witness who saw liquid at 2:55 p.m. or video showing when it appeared can address duration. A cleaning log or employee report can address inspection or actual notice. Give each item its own time, source, and limits. If video may exist, ask promptly about preserving the relevant time window.

The [Insurance Claim Timeline Builder](/tools/claim-timeline-builder) can order the entries. Use the [Accident Photo Checklist](/tools/photo-documentation-planner) to identify views you still need. Keep the initial incident description, later photographs, witness observations, and medical records in their original forms.

## Connect the injury and losses to your records

Keep the first evaluation, follow-up instructions, and records of changes in work or daily tasks. Match provider bills with the corresponding EOB and payments before adding costs. The [lost wages guide](/articles/lost-wages-claims-how-to-calculate-and-maximize-your-compensation-in-2026) explains how to compare missed shifts with actual pay. A claim review should consider the evidence of the hazard and the evidence of the injury separately. [CMS guidance on bills and explanations of benefits](https://www.cms.gov/initiatives/your-patient-rights/medical-bill-rights/get-help/guides-resources/how-read-your-bill)

title: Medical Malpractice Questions: Records, Standard of Care, and Deadlines
content:
An unexpected outcome can raise questions about what happened and whether the care met the applicable professional standard. The injury, the care at issue, and the connection between them need separate evidence. Florida, for example, defines a prevailing professional standard of care in its medical negligence statute. California's courts describe the need to prove both inadequate care and that it caused harm. [Florida Statutes § 766.102](https://flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2026/766.102) · [California Courts medical malpractice guide](https://www.selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/civil-lawsuit/medical-malpractice)

## Identify the question a record can answer

- **Diagnosis and follow-up.** Compare when symptoms were reported, when a test was ordered, when the result was available, and what was communicated afterward.
- **Procedure or medication.** Identify the procedure or medication, date, order, and administration record. Compare the instructions given before and after the visit.
- **Consent.** Preserve the consent form and records about what was discussed. A signature and the actual conversation can address different questions.
- **Harm and later care.** Record the symptoms, follow-up evaluations, and treatment the later clinicians documented. Keep later conclusions separate from the original visit record.

Request the relevant records from the appropriate covered provider or plan. HHS explains that the right of access covers much health and billing information in designated record sets, subject to exceptions. Ask which document and date range the provider can supply. The [Medical Records Tracker](/tools/care-record-gap-view) can help identify missing visits or reports. [HHS guidance on access to health information](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/what-personal-health-information-do-individuals/index.html)

## Build a chronology before assessing causation

For example, a delayed-result question can have four dates: the test order, the lab result, the clinician's documented review, and the patient's follow-up. A result date alone may leave the communication question open. Keep original copies and the source of any date you add. A qualified reviewer can assess the care and what would likely have happened under different circumstances. [California Courts medical malpractice guide](https://www.selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/civil-lawsuit/medical-malpractice)

## Check for procedures before filing

Special rules can apply. Florida's medical negligence law provides for presuit investigation and notice, including a corroborating expert opinion under the statute's terms. California's courts explain its own timing and notice rules. These are state examples. Verify the applicable dates and procedures early, especially if a public healthcare entity may be involved. [Florida Statutes §§ 766.106](https://flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2026/766.106) and [766.203](https://flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2026/766.203) · [California Courts medical malpractice guide](https://www.selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/civil-lawsuit/medical-malpractice)

Use the [filing deadline guide](/articles/statute-of-limitations-for-personal-injury-claims-a-complete-2026-guide-by-state) to separate notice, lawsuit filing, and other clocks. Bring your chronology, actual records, and open questions to a [first consultation](/articles/free-case-evaluation-what-to-expect-from-your-first-attorney-consultation-in-2026). For ongoing symptoms or treatment decisions, contact an appropriate healthcare professional.

title: Workers’ Compensation After an Injury: Claims, Care, and Pay
content:
Workers' compensation procedures depend on the employer, job, and jurisdiction. State programs handle most private-sector employment claims, while federal workers and some other groups may have separate programs. Start with the agency responsible for your employment and the employer's reporting process. [U.S. Department of Labor directory of state workers’ compensation officials](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/owcp/wc)

## Report the injury and keep proof of the claim

Obtain necessary care and report the injury through the employer's process promptly. Write down when and how you reported it, who received the report, and what form you were given. Ask where to file and how to keep proof of receipt. In California, the Division of Workers' Compensation describes a DWC 1 claim form and instructs workers to retain a copy. Follow the process that applies to your job and state. [California DWC claim filing guide](https://www.dir.ca.gov/dwc/FileAClaim.htm)

For an injury that developed over time, document when symptoms affected work and when you reported or learned of a possible work connection. Keep the employer's and clinician's dates separate. Confirm any deadline with its source. Use the [Insurance Claim Timeline Builder](/tools/claim-timeline-builder) to organize the record.

## Separate care, wage benefits, and restrictions

California's workers' compensation guide describes medical care, temporary disability payments for qualifying wage loss, and other benefits. A claims administrator and state rules may determine the treatment process, including provider selection. In California that can depend on predesignation and network arrangements. Ask which treatment and claim procedures apply before relying on a general rule. [California DWC injured worker guidebook](https://www.dir.ca.gov/InjuredWorkerGuidebook/InjuredWorkerGuidebook.html) · [California DWC medical care guidance](https://www.dir.ca.gov/dwc/MedicalCare.htm)

If you receive a return-to-work restriction, keep the dated note, proposed duties, actual hours, and pay stubs together. Temporary disability benefits and the wages you would have earned are different amounts. The [Return-to-Work Hours and Pay Calculator](/tools/phased-return-work-planner) compares schedule scenarios. The [lost wages guide](/articles/lost-wages-claims-how-to-calculate-and-maximize-your-compensation-in-2026) explains how to document actual pay changes. [California DWC temporary disability guidance](https://www.dir.ca.gov/dwc/TemporaryDisability.htm)

## Identify disputes and separate processes

If the claim is denied or treatment is disputed, ask for the written decision, reason, review process, and deadline. Identify the agency that handles the issue. Workplace safety or retaliation complaints can have separate procedures from a benefits dispute. OSHA explains how to report hazards and retaliation under the laws it administers. [OSHA complaint guidance](https://www.osha.gov/workers/file-complaint)

When equipment or a different company's conduct contributed to an injury, a third-party claim may need separate review. The [construction accident guide](/articles/construction-accident-claims-workers-comp-vs-personal-injury-lawsuit-in-2026) shows how to distinguish a workers' compensation file from a possible civil claim involving another party.
