title: Truck Accident Claims: Carrier Records, Coverage, and Evidence
content:
A truck can carry one company's name on its door, another company's trailer, and a load arranged by a third business. Start by identifying what each business did on the trip. Keep the tractor and trailer identifiers, carrier name, USDOT number, and any trip or shipment number in separate fields. FMCSA's public snapshot can help identify a registered carrier and its reported operations. Treat it as a lead and verify who ran the trip. [FMCSA Company Snapshot](https://safer.fmcsa.dot.gov/CompanySnapshot.aspx)

## Identify the decision each record can explain

- A dispatch message or rate confirmation may identify the assignment, timing, and parties who arranged the load. 
- A driver log and supporting records can help establish time on duty and time driving. Compare them with dispatch and location data for the same trip.
- An inspection or maintenance record may show when someone observed a defect and what they did next. Match the unit number to the vehicle involved.

Federal hours-of-service rules differ by operation. For covered property-carrying drivers, FMCSA describes an ordinary 11-hour driving limit after 10 consecutive hours off duty and a 14-hour window, with exceptions. Check which rule applied on the trip before labeling a log entry a violation. A regulatory issue and the cause of a crash are distinct questions. [FMCSA hours-of-service summary](https://www.fmcsa.dot.gov/regulations/hours-service/summary-hours-service-regulations)

## Preserve original files and their time references

Record the carrier, investigator, or agency holding each file and request appropriate preservation promptly. Save the original format and any export notes. A truck module's recorded event may have a different trigger from the first visible impact. The [Swanton toll plaza investigation](/articles/why-time-zero-matters-in-a-truck-crash-black-box-report) illustrates why time zero can mark a different event across sources.

Use the [Claim Evidence Organizer](/tools/evidence-to-fact-map) to connect each observation to its original source. A checksum can help identify whether two copies have the same bytes. The [SHA-256 File Checksum Tool](/tools/evidence-file-fingerprints) computes that value locally. A matching checksum says nothing about when the original recording was made.

## Read the applicable insurance filing and policy separately

FMCSA's filing table uses operation type, vehicle weight, and cargo. For example, it lists a $750,000 minimum for a for-hire property carrier operating vehicles of at least 10,001 pounds GVWR that transports nonhazardous property. Other operations can have different requirements. Use the applicable policy and filings to establish the actual coverage in a case. [FMCSA insurance filing requirements](https://www.fmcsa.dot.gov/registration/insurance-filing-requirements)

If a freight broker arranged the load, separate the driver's conduct from the broker's selection decision. The [Montgomery freight broker case](/articles/can-a-freight-broker-be-sued-after-a-truck-crash) explains how a federal preemption question can be resolved before a court reaches the underlying negligence evidence. Bring a trip-specific timeline, policy documents, and a list of missing records to any review of the claim.

title: Motorcycle Accident Claims: Evidence, Gear, and Coverage
content:
After a motorcycle crash, take care of injuries and leave scene documentation to responders or someone who can help safely. When records are available, separate the collision evidence from the condition of the motorcycle and gear afterward. NHTSA's rider safety guidance explains why visibility, protective equipment, and motorist awareness are important. In an individual claim, the evidence must describe what happened on that ride. [NHTSA motorcycle safety](https://www.nhtsa.gov/road-safety/motorcycles)

## Capture what the rider and the other driver could see

Record the lane position, signal phase, road surface, obstruction, and direction of travel. If the crash involved a turning driver, identify the point where the turn crossed the rider's path and each witness's vantage point. A photograph after traffic cleared may help with geometry. Give it its own date and describe any difference from the scene at the time. Original video and the scene diagram can provide additional checks. [California Department of Insurance crash documentation guide](https://www.insurance.ca.gov/01-consumers/105-type/95-guides/01-auto/hadaccident.cfm)

Preserve the motorcycle and any relevant damaged gear in their existing condition while you arrange appropriate inspection. Photograph visible damage, serial numbers, and labels if safe. Keep ownership documents and any replacement receipts. The [Damaged Property Inventory](/tools/damaged-belongings-inventory) separates documented purchase cost from replacement estimates. Those figures may differ from the valuation under the policy.

## Check which policy applies to the bike, the rider, and equipment

Ask for the motorcycle policy and endorsements, with definitions of insured vehicles, riders, and covered equipment. A coverage label on an auto policy is only a starting point for a motorcycle question. If the other driver's insurer accepts responsibility for a loss, still ask which item the offer covers and what it would release. For policy concepts such as collision and underinsured motorist coverage, start with the [California insurance department's coverage guide](https://www.insurance.ca.gov/01-consumers/105-type/95-guides/01-auto/auto101.cfm), then use the policy and state rules that apply.

Keep the motorcycle estimate separate from medical charges and missed work. If the shop submits a supplement, save both versions. If a part might be defective or recalled, record the vehicle identification number and model, then use the [NHTSA recall lookup](https://www.nhtsa.gov/recalls). A recall search is one evidence check. See the [Ford product-liability case](/articles/why-ford-could-be-sued-where-the-crash-happened) for a separate question about where a defect claim can be heard.

If side cases or racks are absent from the estimate, pair the accessory part numbers and mounting photos with the policy endorsement. [How to document damaged aftermarket panniers](/articles/motorcycle-claim-damaged-aftermarket-panniers).

## Make the injury record specific

Use dated clinical notes, work restrictions, bills, and actual payment records. Describe changes in specific activities, such as putting on a jacket, walking to a bus stop, or lifting a work tool. The [daily activity journal](/tools/daily-function-journal) can help you record comparable observations across days. The [guide to documenting pain and suffering](/articles/how-much-is-my-pain-and-suffering-worth-a-complete-calculation-guide-for-2026) explains why the frequency and duration of those changes matter more than a generic injury multiplier.

title: Uber and Lyft Accidents: Which Insurance Applies?
content:
After a rideshare crash, save the trip receipt, pickup and drop-off information, and any report confirmation. The timestamp that matters for coverage can be the moment the crash happened relative to when the driver went online, accepted the trip, or ended it. A driver's platform membership alone cannot establish the status at the time of a crash. The companies publish coverage summaries organized by these stages. [Uber insurance summary](https://www.uber.com/us/en/drive/insurance/?_pec=no) · [Lyft insurance resources](https://www.lyft.com/driver/insurance)

## Start with the app status at the time of impact

- **Offline.** Check the driver's policy, crash report, and trip history. Ask which personal or commercial policy covered the use of the car.
- **Online and waiting.** Compare the app activity log or dispatch record with the crash time. Ask what liability coverage applied while the driver was available.
- **Ride accepted or underway.** Match the trip receipt and platform report to the acceptance and trip timestamps. Ask which policy and limits were in force for that trip.

Coverage is state- and policy-specific. California's regulator distinguishes the time spent waiting online, the trip to pick up a matched passenger, and the time with the passenger in the vehicle. The platform's current state disclosure and the actual policy or certificate help identify the applicable limits, endorsements, and exclusions. Keep liability, uninsured or underinsured motorist coverage, and damage to the driver's vehicle on separate lines. [California Public Utilities Commission TNC insurance requirements](https://www.cpuc.ca.gov/regulatory-services/licensing/transportation-licensing-and-analysis-branch/transportation-network-companies/tnc-insurance-requirements) · [Lyft state and local disclosures](https://www.lyft.com/terms/disclosures)

## Match your role to your claim number

A passenger can usually identify the trip from the receipt. Preserve it and report through the platform's crash process. If you were in another vehicle or walking, your starting evidence may be the driver's identity, police report, and insurer correspondence rather than a trip receipt. A rideshare driver should also preserve app activity and any rideshare endorsement to a personal policy. When two apps may have been open, record the evidence for each app separately and ask each insurer to identify the period it evaluated.

For each claim number, record the insurer, the specific coverage under review, and which documents it requested. The [Insurance Claim Contact Log](/tools/claim-contact-ledger) keeps multiple contacts from becoming one running conversation. The [work-vehicle underinsured motorist case](/articles/can-your-auto-policy-cover-a-crash-in-a-work-car) illustrates why an employer or vehicle policy and a personal policy can produce different answers.

A driver who missed a promotion threshold can document the offered terms, eligible trip count and comparable shifts separately from the usual trip earnings. [How to document a missed weekly rideshare bonus](/articles/missed-rideshare-weekly-bonus-after-crash).

## Keep the injury and repair records separate

A statement about third-party liability coverage may leave your medical payments, deductibles, and repair expenses unresolved. Ask which payment covers which loss, whether it is subject to a limit or deductible, and what the insurer needs to confirm eligibility. For a scene and reporting checklist, see [what to do after a car accident](/articles/what-to-do-after-a-car-accident-a-complete-step-by-step-guide). If an insurer denies a coverage layer, use the [denied claim guide](/articles/how-to-fight-a-denied-insurance-claim-and-win) to compare its written reason with the applicable policy.

title: Pain and Suffering in Injury Claims: What Evidence Matters?
content:
Pain and suffering describes types of harm that may include physical discomfort, emotional distress, and loss of enjoyment of life. The categories and rules depend on the claim and jurisdiction. In California, the general civil jury instruction CACI 3905A asks jurors to assess a reasonable amount from the evidence and their judgment. It supplies no fixed formula for noneconomic damages. [California Civil Jury Instructions, CACI 3905A](https://courts.ca.gov/system/files/file/judicial_council_of_california_civil_jury_instructions_2026.pdf#page=2759)

## Replace adjectives with dates and activities

Compare a specific activity before and after the injury. If someone used to carry groceries upstairs, note how often, what help they need now, and the date of each relevant observation. A clinician's lifting restriction, a follow-up note, and a household member's own observation can describe different parts of that change. Label each record by its source.

For repeated observations, use comparable tasks and note both easier and more difficult days. Record practical details such as duration, time needed for a break, assistance, and symptoms already discussed with a healthcare provider. Use the [Daily Activity Recovery Journal](/tools/daily-function-journal) to organize entries without treating a personal difficulty score as a medical assessment or dollar amount.

## Explain past effects and future effects separately

A past change has dates you can document. A future claim depends on evidence about expected duration or continuing effects. Keep medical opinions and care recommendations separate from personal predictions. California's instruction distinguishes past and future damages and addresses the proof for future noneconomic harm. [California Civil Jury Instructions, CACI 3905A](https://courts.ca.gov/system/files/file/judicial_council_of_california_civil_jury_instructions_2026.pdf#page=2759)

When a photo or post seems inconsistent with a restriction, save the original context, date, and what the activity actually involved. The [Forman social media case](/articles/when-private-social-media-becomes-injury-case-evidence) illustrates how a court can order targeted disclosure based on what matters in a particular injury claim. A caption, timestamp, and account of the event can each provide a different piece of evidence.

## Read a settlement offer alongside the evidence

An offer may combine different losses in one amount. Ask what it resolves and which facts the insurer disputes. For the arithmetic, keep actual medical and wage expenses separate from the description of pain and changes in daily activity. The [settlement breakdown guide](/articles/how-much-is-my-car-accident-settlement-worth-in-2025-complete-guide) and [offer comparison tool](/tools/offer-net-comparison) help with written amounts and deductions. Bring the activity record to the same review so the scope of the release and the actual harm are considered together. [California Courts overview of personal injury cases](https://www.selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/civil-lawsuit/personal-injury)

title: Seven Recordkeeping Mistakes That Can Complicate an Injury Claim
content:
An injury file is easier to review when another person can tell what happened, when it happened, and which source supports each statement. These seven common gaps are practical places to start.

## Losing the report reference

Write down the agency, report number, and date. Keep a state reporting form, police report, and insurer claim reference separate. Different reports can serve different purposes. See the [post-crash checklist](/articles/what-to-do-after-a-car-accident-a-complete-step-by-step-guide) for what to capture safely. [California Department of Insurance crash reporting guide](https://www.insurance.ca.gov/01-consumers/105-type/95-guides/01-auto/hadaccident.cfm)

## Saving only edited copies

Keep original photos, videos, and messages with their dates. Use separate copies for crops or redactions. Identify who took a photo and whether it shows the incident or a later visit. The [Accident Photo Checklist](/tools/photo-documentation-planner) helps group the views. [NAIC auto claim documentation guide](https://content.naic.org/article/what-you-should-know-about-filing-auto-claim)

## Leaving medical and work dates unexplained

Seek medical care when needed and follow the clinical guidance you receive. Keep dates of symptoms, visits, restrictions, and missed work. Some concussion symptoms can appear later. Discuss relevant changes with a healthcare provider. The [lost wages guide](/articles/lost-wages-claims-how-to-calculate-and-maximize-your-compensation-in-2026) shows how to match restrictions and actual pay records. [CDC mild TBI symptoms guidance](https://www.cdc.gov/traumatic-brain-injury/signs-symptoms/index.html)

## Treating private posts as outside the record

Preserve relevant posts and messages in context. Changing visibility or deleting material can create separate issues when evidence needs to be preserved. In New York's *Forman v. Henkin*, the court considered targeted disclosure based on relevance to the injuries and limitations claimed. See the [social media evidence case](/articles/when-private-social-media-becomes-injury-case-evidence) for what was ordered and why. [New York Court of Appeals opinion](https://www.nycourts.gov/Reporter/3dseries/2018/2018_01015.htm)

## Giving a guess the status of a fact

If you cannot remember speed, distance, or timing, say so. Date any correction and explain its source. Ask what a recorded statement is for and whether your policy requires it. The [adjuster conversation guide](/articles/what-to-say-and-what-never-to-say-to-insurance-adjusters-after-an-accident-in-2026) offers neutral ways to make the next step clear. [NAIC claim communication guidance](https://content.naic.org/article/what-you-should-know-about-filing-auto-claim)

## Comparing gross offers alone

Ask for the release and written breakdown. Identify which claims the payment resolves and what costs or repayments may come out of it. Compare scenarios using the [Net Settlement Offer Comparison tool](/tools/offer-net-comparison). [California State Bar guidance on fees and costs](https://www.calbar.ca.gov/public/legal-resources/working-attorney/what-expect-regarding-fees-and-billing) · [CMS beneficiary recovery process](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/coordination-benefits-recovery/beneficiary-services/recovery-process)

## Combining all dates into one reminder

A time to respond to an offer, a policy notice, and a lawsuit filing date are different entries. Put the source beside each confirmed date, using the [Insurance Claim Date and Reminder Planner](/tools/important-date-planner) if helpful. Check the [filing deadline guide](/articles/statute-of-limitations-for-personal-injury-claims-a-complete-2026-guide-by-state) for examples of separate legal and government notice clocks. [California Courts filing deadline guide](https://selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/civil-lawsuit/statute-limitations)

title: When to Speak With a Personal Injury Lawyer
content:
A useful consultation starts with a decision you need to make. You might have a release to review, a denial to challenge, a defendant to identify, or a deadline you cannot confirm. Write down the decision and the document behind it. Courts and state bars describe different ways to find help, and a certified referral service can direct you to a practice area. [State Bar of California lawyer referral directory](https://www.calbar.ca.gov/public/find-legal-professionals/find-lawyer-referral-service)

## Seek clarity when a deadline or release is involved

A government claim, a medical negligence claim, and an ordinary personal injury suit may have different notice or filing requirements. If a city vehicle, public property, or public facility was involved, identify the responsible entity early. Ask which date starts each clock and what must be delivered to whom. [California Courts deadline guide](https://selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/civil-lawsuit/statute-limitations) · [California Courts government claim guide](https://selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/civil-lawsuit/government-claim)

If you received an offer, bring the proposed release and written terms. Ask which claims and people it covers, what is paid and when, and who is responsible for unpaid bills or asserted repayments. See [how to compare a settlement with litigation](/articles/settlement-vs-trial-which-path-to-choose-for-your-personal-injury-case-in-2026) for the issues behind the gross figure. [California State Bar guide to fees and costs](https://www.calbar.ca.gov/public/legal-resources/working-attorney/what-expect-regarding-fees-and-billing)

## Bring focused records when fault, coverage, or losses are disputed

When several companies may be involved, identify their roles and the record connecting each to the event. A truck crash may involve a carrier, driver, owner, or broker whose conduct raises separate issues. A work-vehicle claim can involve an employer's policy and personal coverage with different terms. The [truck crash guide](/articles/truck-accident-claims-why-18-wheeler-crashes-are-fundamentally-different-in-2026) and [work-car coverage case](/articles/can-your-auto-policy-cover-a-crash-in-a-work-car) show how to keep those questions separate. [FMCSA company safety records](https://www.fmcsa.dot.gov/safety/company-safety-records)

If the injury affects work or requires future care, bring work restrictions, wage records, treatment recommendations, and any cost estimates. Keep present costs distinct from future assumptions. The [Claim Evidence Organizer](/tools/evidence-to-fact-map) can link each issue to its source so the lawyer can identify gaps during the meeting. [California Civil Jury Instructions, damages series](https://courts.ca.gov/system/files/file/judicial_council_of_california_civil_jury_instructions_2026.pdf#page=2695)

## Prepare for a decision at the end of the meeting

Ask what the lawyer would investigate first, what you can do next, and what would happen only after hiring them. Confirm how fees and costs work under the written terms. The [first consultation guide](/articles/free-case-evaluation-what-to-expect-from-your-first-attorney-consultation-in-2026) lists documents and questions that make the meeting easier to use. Bring the exact denial, deadline notice, or proposed release if it prompted the call.

title: Whiplash Claims: Neck Injury Records and Settlement Factors
content:
Whiplash can occur when the head and neck move suddenly, as in a collision. Neck pain has multiple possible causes. A medical evaluation can document the symptoms, findings, and follow-up appropriate to the injury. If a crash also involved a head injury, symptoms such as repeated vomiting, seizures, or worsening headache that does not go away warrant immediate emergency care under CDC guidance. [MedlinePlus overview of whiplash](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/imagepages/9853.htm) · [CDC head-injury danger signs](https://www.cdc.gov/traumatic-brain-injury/signs-symptoms/index.html)

## Make the early and follow-up records agree on the dates

Record when the crash happened, when each symptom first appeared, and when you discussed it with a clinician. Keep separate entries for the collision report, exam, referral, therapy, and any written work restriction. A later clinician can explain whether the course of symptoms and findings support a diagnosis. Use the [Medical Records Tracker](/tools/care-record-gap-view) to see which visit summaries or referrals are still missing. [HHS guidance on access to health records](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/what-personal-health-information-do-individuals/index.html)

Where your work or activities changed, describe a particular task and date. For example, turning your head repeatedly on a job, carrying tools, or sitting through a commute may each present different difficulties. Keep contemporaneous notes and relevant work records. The [lost wages guide](/articles/lost-wages-claims-how-to-calculate-and-maximize-your-compensation-in-2026) explains how to distinguish missed work from paid leave.

## Reconcile charges before discussing a settlement amount

A provider's bill, an EOB, and a payment receipt each answer a different question. For each service, record the date, provider, and claim reference. Add the plan's stated patient responsibility and payments already made, then compare the result with the provider's requested balance. If an EOB shows $180 due and you already paid $60 toward that service, the simple remaining amount is $120 under those assumptions. Ask for an explanation if the bill differs. [CMS guide to reading a medical bill](https://www.cms.gov/initiatives/your-patient-rights/medical-bill-rights/get-help/guides-resources/how-read-your-bill)

## Review the offer against the evidence

A diagnosis by itself does not supply a reliable settlement amount. Coverage, responsibility for the crash, documented treatment and wage effects, and any ongoing limitations can change the assessment. If an offer combines several losses, request a written breakdown and the release language. For noneconomic harm, California's civil jury instructions illustrate an evidence-based assessment without a fixed multiplier. [California Civil Jury Instructions, CACI 3905A](https://courts.ca.gov/system/files/file/judicial_council_of_california_civil_jury_instructions_2026.pdf#page=2759)

Compare the offer with your records and confirmed deductions using the [Net Settlement Calculator](/tools/settlement-net-waterfall). The [car accident settlement breakdown](/articles/how-much-is-my-car-accident-settlement-worth-in-2025-complete-guide) explains which amounts to keep separate. The [pain and suffering guide](/articles/how-much-is-my-pain-and-suffering-worth-a-complete-calculation-guide-for-2026) shows how to record changes in day-to-day activities without turning them into a formula.

title: Five Insurance Adjuster Requests Worth Clarifying
content:
An adjuster can ask for records, explain policy terms, and communicate offers. The same request may mean something different depending on whose insurer is asking and which part of the claim is being evaluated. A useful response identifies the specific document, deadline, and coverage rather than guessing why someone asked. [NAIC auto claim guidance](https://content.naic.org/article/what-you-should-know-about-filing-auto-claim)

## An early offer

Ask which losses the payment resolves and request the proposed release. A repair payment, a bodily injury offer, and a proposed full release should have separate entries in your file. If treatment or a repayment demand is unresolved, identify what remains open and who would bear it under the proposed terms. [California insurance department auto claims guide](https://www.insurance.ca.gov/01-consumers/105-type/95-guides/01-auto/hadaccident.cfm) · [CMS beneficiary recovery process](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/coordination-benefits-recovery/beneficiary-services/recovery-process)

## A request to record your account

Ask what topics it covers, who will receive the recording, and how to request a copy. If the request comes from your insurer, check any applicable duty under the policy. Give accurate facts and label what you do not remember. The [guide to talking with an adjuster](/articles/what-to-say-and-what-never-to-say-to-insurance-adjusters-after-an-accident-in-2026) offers ways to answer and confirm the next step.

## Permission to obtain records

Ask for the purpose, record type, dates, and recipients. You may need to provide a particular report or authorization depending on the coverage, request, and procedural setting. Save the actual document you signed. HHS's access guidance explains how individuals can generally obtain their own health records from covered entities, subject to exceptions. [HHS right to access health information](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/what-personal-health-information-do-individuals/index.html)

## A deduction from a valuation

Ask what changed between the comparable vehicle and your vehicle, what evidence supports the adjustment, and where the dollar amount appears in the report. Keep the condition deduction separate from the deductible, taxes, and other lines. The [Washington total-loss case](/articles/what-the-condition-adjustment-does-to-a-total-loss-offer) shows how to read a condition adjustment. The [Deduction Question Builder](/tools/deduction-question-builder) helps turn each unexplained line into a written question.

## An update that says the claim is still under review

Ask what issue is pending, what item is missing, and when you should expect the next communication. Keep a dated record of requests and replies. California publishes specific claim-handling rules through its insurance department. The exact obligations depend on the state and claim. [California fair claims settlement regulations](https://www.insurance.ca.gov/01-consumers/130-laws-regs-hearings/05-CCR/fair-claims-regs.cfm)

Paste a short, redacted message into the [Insurance Letter Phrase Checker](/tools/insurance-phrase-decoder) to generate neutral follow-up questions. If the insurer gives conflicting reasons or repeatedly leaves a material issue unresolved, see [how to document a possible claim-handling problem](/articles/how-to-deal-with-insurance-bad-faith-your-complete-2026-action-guide).

title: How to Challenge an Insurance Claim Denial
content:
Read the written denial and identify the claim number, date, coverage, and precise reason. Ask for any cited policy provision and supporting explanation you do not have. A document request, a partial payment, and a final denial can require different responses. Keep copies of the policy and each communication. [NAIC guide to claim documentation](https://content.naic.org/article/what-you-should-know-about-filing-auto-claim)

## Match the evidence to the reason

- **A required document is missing.** Compare the insurer's request with the document and proof of delivery.
- **The policy excludes the loss.** Read the declarations, applicable policy version, and endorsements together.
- **The amount or cause is disputed.** Check the itemized estimate, photographs, written valuation, or professional report behind the disputed figure.
- **A health plan denies a service.** Match the EOB and denial to the plan language and any provider explanation.

Respond to the specific reason. If an EOB says a health claim was processed a certain way, verify the service date and billing entity before comparing it with a provider's statement. The [Compare a Medical Bill With Your EOB tool](/tools/medical-bill-eob-reconciler) organizes those amounts. An EOB and a bill serve different roles. [CMS guide to reading an EOB](https://www.cms.gov/initiatives/your-patient-rights/medical-bill-rights/get-help/guides-resources/read-explanation-benefits)

## Follow the applicable review procedure

For auto or property insurance, use the claim or policy process described by the insurer and check the state insurance department's rules. Ask where to send your response, what review is available, and what date it is due. Keep a copy of the response and its receipt. [NAIC guide to filing an insurance complaint](https://content.naic.org/consumer/how-to-file-complaint)

For health plans subject to applicable appeal protections, the denial notice may describe an internal appeal and external review. Some urgent situations have expedited processes. Verify your plan's applicable procedure and dates before filing. [HealthCare.gov internal appeals](https://www.healthcare.gov/appeal-insurance-company-decision/internal-appeals/) · [CMS action plan for a denied health insurance claim](https://www.cms.gov/initiatives/your-patient-rights/medical-bill-rights/get-help/find-action-plan/health-insurance-plan-denied-claim)

## Write a short response that can be checked

State the decision you are asking the insurer to reconsider, the reason it gave, the record that addresses that reason, and the action you are requesting. List attachments by date and title. If the issue is an inaccurate balance, include only the relevant comparison and ask for a corrected written decision. The [Insurance Claim Follow-Up Email Builder](/tools/claim-follow-up-composer) provides a draft you can review and adjust.

If the insurer leaves a material question unanswered, use the [Insurance Complaint Organizer](/tools/insurance-complaint-packet) to prepare a factual record for the regulator. See [when a denial may raise a bad-faith question](/articles/bad-faith-insurance-what-to-do-when-your-insurance-company-refuses-to-pay-in-2026) for the distinction between challenging the coverage decision and evaluating the conduct behind it. Keep [legal and notice deadlines](/articles/statute-of-limitations-for-personal-injury-claims-a-complete-2026-guide-by-state) separate from your review requests.

title: What to Do After a Car Accident: A Practical Checklist
content:
The first useful record starts with safety. Call 911 for injuries or a dangerous scene and follow the dispatcher's instructions. Move yourself or the vehicle only when you can do so safely and local rules permit it. Exchange the information required where you are, and obtain the responding agency's report number. [California Department of Insurance crash guide](https://www.insurance.ca.gov/01-consumers/105-type/95-guides/01-auto/hadaccident.cfm)

## At the scene, capture what can change

Photograph the vehicle positions if safe, then the lanes, signals, road surface, visible damage, and nearby signs. Take a wide photo and a closer one of the same feature. Keep the original files. Ask witnesses for contact information and a brief account of where they were when they saw the crash. Record a partial plate or camera location while it is fresh if a driver leaves. See [what to preserve after a hit-and-run](/articles/hit-and-run-accident-what-to-do-who-pays-and-how-to-protect-your-rights-in-2026) for identification and coverage questions.

Write the event down while you remember it, separating what you saw from what another person told you. If you later obtain a report, add it with its own date and source. The [Insurance Claim Timeline Builder](/tools/claim-timeline-builder) sorts those entries and leaves the source visible beside each one. [NAIC guidance on documenting an auto claim](https://content.naic.org/article/what-you-should-know-about-filing-auto-claim)

## Open the claim and save the coverage questions

Notify the appropriate insurer under the policy's reporting terms. Ask for the claim number, assigned adjuster, inspection process, and any forms they need. Check whether a state crash report is also required. A police report and an insurer's claim number serve different purposes. In California, the insurance department's guide describes a separate DMV report for certain crashes, including those involving an injury. [California Department of Insurance reporting guidance](https://www.insurance.ca.gov/01-consumers/105-type/95-guides/01-auto/hadaccident.cfm)

Before authorizing repairs, ask who can inspect the car, how the shop handles supplemental damage found after disassembly, and what paperwork confirms any rental allowance. Save the original estimate, revised estimates, and rental dates. If the insurer treats the car as a total loss, ask for the valuation report and the comparable vehicles used. The [total-loss condition-adjustment case](/articles/what-the-condition-adjustment-does-to-a-total-loss-offer) shows how to review one line that changes the offer.

If the report mentions suspected impairment, keep the incident report, any later test result, and the court disposition under separate dates. The [DUI accident claim guide](/articles/dui-accident-claims-in-2026-how-drunk-driving-affects-your-settlement-value) explains what each can establish.

## Match care, charges, and payments

Seek medical care when needed and follow the clinician's instructions. Some concussion symptoms can appear hours or days after an injury. CDC lists danger signs that warrant emergency care, including a worsening headache that does not go away, repeated vomiting, and unusual confusion after a head injury. [CDC concussion symptoms and danger signs](https://www.cdc.gov/traumatic-brain-injury/signs-symptoms/index.html)

If neck symptoms affect your routine, the [whiplash documentation guide](/articles/average-whiplash-settlement-amounts-in-2025-what-your-neck-injury-is-really-worth) shows how to connect each visit, work restriction, and bill to the relevant date.

Keep the itemized bill, explanation of benefits, and payments for the same service together. An EOB explains the plan's handling of the claim. A provider bill requests payment. If the balance differs after accounting for payments, ask the provider to identify the charge or adjustment causing the difference. The [medical bill and EOB tool](/tools/medical-bill-eob-reconciler) helps compare these amounts. [CMS guide to reading your medical bill](https://www.cms.gov/initiatives/your-patient-rights/medical-bill-rights/get-help/guides-resources/how-read-your-bill)

## Before resolving any part of the claim

Ask for the proposed payment and release in writing. Identify the losses it covers, whether it closes injury or property claims, and what expenses or repayments remain. If you need to compare a property offer and an injury offer, keep them in separate rows. The [guide to car accident settlement amounts](/articles/how-much-is-my-car-accident-settlement-worth-in-2025-complete-guide) explains how to reconcile those lines before comparing the bottom numbers.

title: Car Accident Settlement Amounts: How to Read an Offer
content:
A settlement offer is easier to evaluate once you can explain each line. Start with the written proposal and identify which person, insurer, coverage, and losses it addresses. A payment to repair a vehicle and a release of bodily injury claims can resolve different issues. Keep the relevant policy, offer, and proposed release together. [California Department of Insurance auto claim guide](https://www.insurance.ca.gov/01-consumers/105-type/95-guides/01-auto/hadaccident.cfm)

## Build the loss record from documents you can check

For medical expenses, group the itemized provider bill, explanation of benefits, and actual payments by service date and provider. Record the billed amount, plan adjustments, and what remains separately. An EOB describes how the plan processed the charge. The provider can explain a remaining balance or payment that has not posted. [CMS medical bill and EOB guidance](https://www.cms.gov/initiatives/your-patient-rights/medical-bill-rights/get-help/guides-resources/how-read-your-bill)

For past missed work, use a schedule, pay rate, employer confirmation, and the dates of any documented restriction. Track paid leave separately. For a future cost, note what care or service it represents, who recommended it, how often it is expected, and the source for the price. The [lost wages guide](/articles/lost-wages-claims-how-to-calculate-and-maximize-your-compensation-in-2026) and [long-term injury cost guide](/articles/catastrophic-injury-compensation-2026-calculating-long-term-costs-and-maximum-recovery) show how to build both records.

Keep repair or valuation documents in a property file. A total-loss report should be read alongside the condition and options recorded for the car. If a comparable vehicle differs, ask what adjustment the insurer made and why. The [Washington total-loss case](/articles/what-the-condition-adjustment-does-to-a-total-loss-offer) explains the difference between a vehicle-condition deduction and the other amounts that may affect a check.

If the collision involved a motorcycle, keep any damaged riding gear and its receipts on separate lines. The [motorcycle claim guide](/articles/motorcycle-accident-claims-in-2026-how-to-maximize-your-settlement-and-protect-your-rights) explains how to document the bike and equipment and check the coverage for each.

## Identify what the offer leaves unresolved

Coverage limits, disputes about fault or causation, and state rules about recoverable damages affect how an offer is evaluated. Read any proposed release for the parties, claims, and time period it covers. For harm such as pain or loss of enjoyment, use records of the activities affected and the duration rather than turning an expense total into a universal multiplier. California's civil jury instructions, for example, direct jurors to evaluate noneconomic loss from the evidence without a fixed calculation. [California Civil Jury Instructions, CACI 3905A](https://courts.ca.gov/system/files/file/judicial_council_of_california_civil_jury_instructions_2026.pdf#page=2759)

## Calculate the net under a written set of assumptions

Suppose an illustrative $40,000 injury offer has an entered $10,000 fee, $1,200 in costs, and a $3,800 confirmed repayment. That leaves $25,000 under those assumptions. If the fee agreement uses a different calculation base, or a repayment remains disputed, change those inputs and keep both scenarios. The example is arithmetic and gives no estimate of a particular claim.

The [Net Settlement Calculator](/tools/settlement-net-waterfall) and [Net Settlement Offer Comparison](/tools/offer-net-comparison) make the deductions visible. Review the [Medicare recovery case](/articles/a-125000-crash-settlement-and-medicares-repayment-demand) if a payment list and a final demand show different amounts. Compare both the proposed net and the terms you would be accepting. [California State Bar guide to fees and costs](https://www.calbar.ca.gov/public/legal-resources/working-attorney/what-expect-regarding-fees-and-billing)
